newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Maize Board submits phasing-out plan.
newsitem.headline: S.African Maize Board submits phasing-out plan.

text.p: South Africa's Maize Board said on Wednesday it had submitted a business plan to government detailing how it will be phased out and setting in motion the final deregulation of the country's maize industry.

Board chairman Vic Mouton said in a statement the plan, submitted to the newly appointed National Agricultural Marketing Council, had been approved by the board and all parties with a direct interest in maize.
Mouton said certain industry functions previously carried out by the board, including laboratory services and the dissemination of market information, would be transferred to other structures.

"The necessary planning for the creation of new structures or the transfer to existing structures to perform these functions is currently under way," he said adding that the board would continue these service until the new structures were ready to handle them.
Mouton said the board would in particular pursue the settlement of legal actions and the collection of outstanding levies.
All market interventions by the Maize Board, which in the current 1996/97 season was still active in the export market, would cease from the start of the new season on May 1.

All South Africa's agricultural control boards face the axe following the passing late last year of the pro-deregulation Marketing of Agricultural Products Act. According to this legislation, boards have 13 months to reshape themselves into market-driven organisations.
